title: A colour test for knots
hook: Can three colours tell a knot from a plain loop?

knows: a knot drawing has gaps where one strand passes under, and 'the same knot' means you can wiggle one into the other without cutting
doesNotKnow: that a colouring rule can separate the trefoil from a plain loop: the trefoil can be coloured with all three colours, a plain loop only with one, and wiggling never changes which of these a knot allows (the last clause is told context; the first two are shown)

misconception: The only way to show a knot can't be undone is to try hard and fail; and if I couldn't colour it, it can't be coloured (one failed try is not a proof).
objective: The learner can explain that the trefoil is not a plain loop because it allows a three-colouring that a plain loop never allows, and that settling 'can't be coloured' takes checking every colouring, not one failed try.

claims.text: The colouring rule: colour every arc (the rope between two gaps) one of three colours; at each crossing the three arcs that meet are all one colour or all different ('Rule: at each crossing, the three arcs (rope between gaps) are all one colour or all different.'). A knot is tricolourable when it has such a colouring using more than one colour. On the stage each crossing shows a solid ring and a tick when its three arcs obey the rule, a dashed ring and a cross when they do not, and the counter 'Crossings OK: n of 3' (n of 4 on 4₁; 'No crossings' on ○).
claims.source: Adams, The Knot Book, section 1.5; Wikipedia 'Tricolorability' (research note company/research/notes/2026-10-13-teachable-knot-theory.md §2.2, high; full text unchecked). Brief claim 1 (company/domains/briefs/math.discrete.md, Knots batch 1, brief 2). The stage applies it with colouringOk(pd, colours, 3) from src/kit/knots (2*over = in + out mod 3, which for p = 3 is all same or all different). The stage counts single-colour colourings as obeying the rule, as colourings() does; the 'more than one colour' condition is carried by the question 'Can the trefoil use all three colours?'. Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: W-1540 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): VERIFIED at 5c5c719e. Rule and definition match PMC12398458 Def. 3.1 word for word in meaning: 'A Fox tricoloring of a knot diagram is a coloring of the strands with three colors such that at each crossing, the colors of the strands that meet at that crossing are either all the same or all different' and 'A knot diagram is called Fox tricolorable if it has a non-trivial tricoloring'; strands there are the pieces between breaks (the lesson's arcs). Kit colouringOk agrees with my own a + c - 2b = 0 mod 3 enumeration on 3_1 and 4_1. Stage: ringOk solid with tick, ringBad stroke-dasharray with cross (styles.module.css), counter text as quoted. Builder should swap the Wikipedia/Adams source (unopened) for PMC12398458. Record: company/reviews/tricolour-check/2026-10-16-fact-check.md

claims.text: A plain loop has one arc, so it can only ever be one colour ('A plain loop has one arc, so it can only ever be one colour.'; stage on ○ after Check all: '○: 3 of 3 obey: all one colour').
claims.source: Definition of arc (no crossings, so no gaps: one arc). K2: colourings([], 3) = 3, one per colour (node company/domains/briefs/checks/knots-check.mjs; builder re-run 2026-10-16 with src/kit/knots: 3). The ○ chip is a plain SVG circle with one arc; census(null, 1) in Demo.tsx gives 3 of 3, all one colour. Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: W-1540 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): VERIFIED at 5c5c719e. A crossing-free circle has one arc; under any rule a single arc takes one colour, so 3 colourings, all one colour; census(null, 1) prints '3 of 3 obey: all one colour'. PMC12398458: the trefoil is tricolorable 'and the former [the unknot] is not'. Record: company/reviews/tricolour-check/2026-10-16-fact-check.md

Tapping its first two arcs once each (staggered cycle) gives colours B, C, A with all 3 crossings OK ('Seen on 3₁: 3 colours, 3 of 3 OK'; reveal: 'The trefoil took all three colours with every crossing obeying the rule.').
claims.source: K2 and K16 (node company/domains/briefs/checks/knots-check.mjs). Builder re-run 2026-10-16 (scratch geom.mjs, the same census and cycle as Demo.tsx on src/kit/knots): colourings(3_1, 3) = 9; enumeration with colouringOk: one 3, two 0, three 6 of 27; taps arc 0 then arc 1 give (1,2,0), 3 of 3 crossings OK, 3 colours used. The seen line and the reveal quote the state recorded when milestone trefoil3 fired. Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: W-1540 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): VERIFIED at 5c5c719e. Own no-kit enumeration on the kit PD [[1,4,2,5],[3,6,4,1],[5,2,6,3]]: 3 arcs, 3 crossings, 9 of 27 obey: 3 one colour, 0 two, 6 all three (kit colourings 9 agrees). Every crossing meets 3 distinct arcs, so any all-three colouring ticks all 3. K16: step(k) = 1 + (k mod 2) from (A,A,A): arc 1 -> B, arc 2 -> C, arc 3 A = (B,C,A), 3 of 3 OK; trefoil3 records colours 3, ok 3 of 3 only under that condition, and the reveal is gated on it. Drawn arcs: each arc is one continuous path (2 edges joined) whose ends stop about 6 units from a crossing. Record: company/reviews/tricolour-check/2026-10-16-fact-check.md

claims.text: Whether a knot can be coloured this way (with more than one colour) does not change when the knot is wiggled without cutting (Reidemeister moves), so the trefoil cannot be wiggled into a plain loop ('Wiggling a knot, without cutting, never changes whether it can be coloured this way, so the trefoil can never be wiggled into a plain loop.'). Told context, not shown on the stage.
claims.source: Theorem (tricolourability is a knot invariant): Wikipedia 'Tricolorability'; Adams, The Knot Book, section 1.5; CEMC Grade 9/10 knot theory problem set (research note §2.2, high; full text unchecked). Brief claim 5. If this claim is held, the brief says cut the sentence and tell cm-math-discrete the lesson has lost its proof. Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: W-1540 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): VERIFIED at 5c5c719e. Source opened: PMC12398458 states 'Tricolorability is another invariant of a knot [51: Przytycki, 3-coloring and other elementary invariants of knots, Banach Center Publ. 42 (1998) 275-295]. This already allows us to distinguish the unknot and trefoil knot, as the latter is tricolorable and the former is not'; its Thm 2.13 (Reidemeister: two diagrams are of the same knot iff related by Reidemeister moves) and Thm 4.7 (equivalent diagrams have Fox colouring spaces of the same dimension; for F_3, t = -1 this is the 3-colourings), with Remark 4.6 (dimension > 1 iff a non-trivial colouring). PMC5582600 (Angew 2017): 'Reidemeister moves allow transitions between any two diagrams (i.e. conformations) of the same knot', which carries 'wiggling without cutting'. For a knot a non-trivial colouring always uses all three colours (no crossing may show exactly two), so 'coloured this way' (all three) equals 'more than one colour'. The proof stays. Builder should swap the source field to these. Record: company/reviews/tricolour-check/2026-10-16-fact-check.md

claims.text: This test cannot tell the figure-eight from a plain loop: neither can be coloured with more than one colour ('That does not make it a plain loop: this test cannot tell the two apart.').
claims.source: K2 (4_1: 3 of 81, all single-colour; plain loop: 3, all single-colour) plus claim c1's definition. Brief claim 6. Not claimed: that the figure-eight is knotted (true, but not shown here). Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: W-1540 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): VERIFIED at 5c5c719e. Own counts: 4_1 3 of 81 all one colour, plain loop 3 all one colour, so the test gives the same answer for both. 'That does not make it a plain loop' is a logical caution; the figure-eight is in fact knotted (det 5; PMC12398458 Fig. 1b 'a non-trivial knot'), so no reading of the sentence is false. Record: company/reviews/tricolour-check/2026-10-16-fact-check.md

recall.question: A knot drawing can be coloured with all three colours under the crossing rule. Can it be wiggled into a plain loop?
options: Yes, if you find the right wiggle
Only if it has fewer than 3 crossings
recall.why: A plain loop can only be one colour, and wiggling never changes whether a knot can be coloured with all three, so no wiggle can turn it into a plain loop.
